core_principles.text: Set up for the push-up in a strict plank position forming a straight line from the head down, with the core tight, hands wider than shoulder-width apart, and feet shoulder-width apart.
Bring the chest to touch the floor at the bottom of the movement without completely disengaging muscle tension.
Press all the way back up to full lockout of the elbows at the top of the movement.
Perform push-up reps with a slow, controlled cadence while keeping the core and glutes engaged throughout the set.

common_mistakes.text: Shortening the range of motion at the bottom of the movement by stopping an inch or two above the floor.
Shortening the range of motion at the top of the movement by failing to come to full elbow lockout.
Prioritizing fast rep speed and higher rep targets over completing full range of motion reps.

specific_findings.text: Enforcing strict full range of motion with chest-to-floor contact and full lockout reduces total rep capacity by approximately 60% compared to performing partial-range reps.

core_principles.text: Lower your chest all the way to the floor on every repetition without disengaging your body at the bottom.
Prioritize repetition quality and movement intensity over chasing higher rep counts.

common_mistakes.text: Failing to complete the full range of motion at the bottom of the repetition to inflate rep numbers.

specific_findings.text: Switching to a full range of motion where the chest reaches the ground can reduce push-up repetition performance by approximately 60%, dropping rep output from 100 down to 40.

consequences.text: Failing to lower the chest completely to the floor reduces the total work required of the upper body, limiting potential strength and muscle development.
